correctness.rationale: Uniform layered permutations are in bijection with independent equiprobable (n-1) binary cut bits, and both orders and the bit predicate are first-order mutually interpretable. Each first-order sentence induces a regular word language; its rational transition Markov chain has rational Cesàro limit and a published convergence theorem identifies the ordinary limit. For any q, the unbordered marker 0^(k+2)1 yields nonoverlapping occurrences separated by >k; immediately following k fair bits are independent across marker stopping times. The first sample <q is uniform on [0,q), giving P(win)=p/q times P(some eligible marker) at every finite word size; the latter tends to 1 by independent disjoint window occurrences. Endpoint p=0,p=q and q=1 are covered. Bundled checker.py source inspected; first-hit mechanism is mathematical proof, not numerical extrapolation.
residual_risks: No reliance on finite checker for the infinite spectrum, which follows from first-hit and regularity proof.
